newsitem.title: FRANCE: France renews support for Boutros against U.S.
newsitem.headline: France renews support for Boutros against U.S.

text.p: France renewed its support for United Nations Secretary-General Boutros Boutros-Ghali on Tuesday after Washington vetoed his re-election for a second five-year term.
"Through his exceptional experience and personal prestige, (Boutros-Ghali) seems to us to be the best qualified person," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.
"Only the veto of a member state prevented his election for a fresh peace mandate."
The United States, standing alone against all other 14 members of the Security Council, vetoed a second term for Boutros-Ghali as secretary-general of the United Nations.
"Consultations are actively continuing with France's participation," the Foreign Ministry said
Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt earlier issued a veiled threat that France could use its own veto in the Security Council against another candidate.
"We have noted that a single country is holding out against the world consensus. It would be interesting to know what kind of solution the United States has in mind," he told reporters.
"France also has veto power, like its four partners," Rummelhardt said. The United States, Britain, France, Russia and China all have veto power on the council.
"We are not there yet," a ministry official later said when asked if France could use its veto.

France, a strong supporter of Boutros-Ghali, insists on a French-speaking U.N. chief and could block any other candidate, particularly one from a so-called "anglophone" country that the United States might favour.

Rummelhardt said that under U.N. procedure, the General Assembly could appoint the secretary-general if no agreement has been reached in the Security Council when Boutros-Ghali's term expires on December 31.
